trust_decision.summary: Each TEE secure-service wrapper (_ss_*) decides whether every REE-supplied pointer and its full length [p, p+len) lie in REE memory before passing it to the M-mode implementation; at the pinned commit the check tests only the start (and one-past-end) addresses with esp_tee_ptr_in_ree, misses many arguments, nested struct pointers and fixed-size outputs, and does not catch wraparound.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'Secure Service Wrappers'. The _ss_* wrappers in esp_secure_services.c open with the AES wrappers and their start/end-only esp_tee_ptr_in_ree checks.

fix_sites.entry_point: shared helper used by every _ss_* service (new esp_tee_buf_in_ree, fix.diff:981-992)
REE esp_tee_sec_storage_ecdsa_sign / get_pubkey / aead_encrypt / aead_decrypt / ecdsa_sign_pbkdf2
REE MMU HAL -> _ss_mmu_hal_map_region / vaddr_to_paddr / paddr_to_vaddr (out pointers)
TEE heap assert (hardening, not a pointer check)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The key-id strings (clear_key key_id, cfg->id, aead ctx->key_id) have no length argument and are only read by NVS by name, so a solver can argue they are 'not a buffer' and not part of the buffer-range check. The example secure service is sample code and not part of the TEE core.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate calls must keep working. AEAD with aad==NULL/aad_len==0 must stay accepted. _ss_esp_sha_dma accepts buf_len==0 with buf unchecked. _ss_esp_ds_finish_sign must accept the TEE-allocated esp_ds_ctx returned by start_sign, which lies in TEE memory, so requiring it to be REE memory breaks DS signing. supports_direct_read/write take a single pointer with no length. Over-strict zero-length rejection also changes the documented error codes the tests expect (INVALID_SIZE -> INVALID_ARG).

O6_input_shapes: end address wraparound / overflow (len > SIZE_MAX - start)
fixed-size outputs whose size is implied by type (digest size by sha_type, DS sig size by rsa_length, 16-byte IV, sizeof(struct))
the context struct pointer itself (ctx, cfg, hal, host, trans, chip)
nested pointers inside REE structs (ctx->input, ctx->aad, ctx->salt, trans->mosi_data/miso_data)
previously unchecked arguments (iv, iv_off, nc_off, point, scalar, out_len, out_paddr)
integer overflow in OTA rel_offset+size bound

O8_uncovered_routes.route: _ss_esp_tee_sec_storage_clear_key passes an unchecked REE key_id string pointer to NVS lookup (strlen/compare reads TEE memory)
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: No length argument; it is a name, not a buffer, and the fix's own hunk leaves it unchanged (fix.diff:413-425)
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the landing point; sink in components/esp_tee/subproject/components/tee_sec_storage/tee_sec_storage.c:265-268

O8_uncovered_routes.route: cfg->id (esp_tee_sec_storage_key_cfg_t) nested string pointer: the fix validates cfg itself but not cfg->id before NVS lookup in gen_key/ecdsa_sign/get_pubkey
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The struct is validated, so the solver considers the job done; it is the same 'name, not buffer' argument

O8_uncovered_routes.route: aead ctx->key_id nested string pointer passed to tee_sec_storage_crypt_common unchecked
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The fix validates ctx, ctx->input and ctx->aad but treats key_id as an identifier

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Example custom secure service dereferences REE ctx/ctx->input/ctx->aad/output/tag with only NULL checks, no REE-range validation
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Example code outside components/, not shipped in the TEE core

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An attestation helper that copies a REE-provided claim/nonce buffer with a start-only check
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Attestation has its own component and _ss_ wrapper. A maintainer adding a new attestation service could copy the old two-point check.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A new MMU/cache service with an out-pointer validated only by its start address
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The neighbouring MMU wrappers at the pinned commit checked only the flash range and never the out pointer, so the pattern is native to this file.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A key derivation helper taking a REE salt/info buffer inside a ctx struct, validated only as the struct
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: PBKDF2 ctx->salt was exactly this case before the fix (fix.diff:595), so a parallel HKDF-style service would plausibly repeat it.

O9_family: TEE/REE boundary pointer-range validation (CWE-125/CWE-20 out-of-bounds read and confused-deputy write via secure-service arguments)

O10_build.toolchain: ESP-IDF (idf.py, CMake/Ninja, riscv32-esp-elf GCC); TEE subproject built for esp32c6/c5/h2-class targets
O10_build.project_tests: components/esp_tee/test_apps/tee_test_fw (Unity on-target tests, pytest-embedded; e.g. main/test_esp_tee_sec_stg.c 'Null Pointer and Zero Length'); these need hardware or QEMU for RISC-V ESP targets. Host-side unit testing of _ss_* would need a custom harness that stubs esp_tee_app_config and the SOC_* memory map.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Replace the two-point esp_tee_ptr_in_ree checks with a range helper in the AES/SHA wrappers that already have checks, and miss the wrappers with no check at all (sha_block/digest_state, wdt, spi host, gen_key), the nested struct pointers, the implied-size outputs and the OTA integer overflow.

out_of_scope_notes: The published fix itself overwrites earlier results: aead aad check uses '=' not '&=' (fix.diff:547-548, 573-574) and ds_sign/start_sign reassign valid_addr after dereferencing data->rsa_length before data is validated (fix.diff:308-310, 321-324). Hidden tests derived from the fix may encode these quirks.

Test-only service _ss_esp_tee_test_priv_mode_switch(uint32_t *a, uint32_t *b) in components/esp_tee/test_apps/tee_test_fw/components/test_sec_srv/src/test_sec_srv.c:39 takes REE pointers; test firmware only.
